lineage_note: Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning SAUCE. Lead is governed by China GB 2762 'Condiments excluding spices' (Pb 1000; china_gb2762_pb_condiments_excl_spices_1000), whose Appendix A.1 explicitly places soy sauce and compound/blended condiments under this line — stricter than the Vietnam QCVN 8-2 generic 'Sauce' Pb 2000. Cadmium and total arsenic are governed by the stricter Uruguay RBN general limit for LIQUID foods (Cd 100, tAs 100; uy_rbn_general_cd_liquid_foods_0_1mgkg / uy_rbn_general_tas_liquid_foods_0_1mgkg), a pourable soy sauce being a liquid food; these bind below the Vietnam 'Sauce' Cd 1000 / tAs 1000 and the Singapore 'tomato ketchup and other sauces' tAs 1000. Total mercury is the Vietnam 'Sauce' value (tHg 50). Soy sauce has a documented lead-contamination history (e.g. Hong Kong recalls), so the ratchet still applies. Nickel is held under a soy-accumulation screen because soybeans concentrate nickel (EU regulates soybean nickel at 15000) and no sovereign sets a sauce nickel ML. Total chromium is held under a reflex screen disclosed against the Hong Kong Cap 132V pulses total-chromium ML (1000), soy sauce being a pulse/legume ferment.
